author: Life in the 1800s
description:
This was filmed on location at the Campus Martius Museum in Marietta, Ohio on March 22, 2026.   Special thanks to the team at the Campus Martius Museum and the Ohio History Connection!  

Rufus Putnam (1738–1824) was an American military engineer, surveyor, and pioneer.  He played a crucial role in the military success of the American Revolution and later helped establish the first permanent American settlement in the Northwest Territory at Marietta. His life demonstrates how engineering skill, military leadership, and frontier vision shaped the early United States.

Soon after arriving in Marietta, Putnam constructed what is now known as the Rufus Putnam House, built in 1788 using a post-and-plank construction method common to New England but adapted for frontier defense. The house served both as a family residence and as part of the settlement’s fortification.
